knowledge:
- key_parameters: dataDirectory=Path to the directory containing raw amplitude .csv files ending with _wellID_amplitude.csv ;; software=The Bio-Rad software used to export data, must be either "QuantaSoft" or "QX Manager" ;; sampleSheetFile=Path to a .csv sample sheet containing Well, Sample, TargetType, and Target columns ;; B=Number of permutations used by the likelihood ratio test (LRT) to decide the number of mixture components (default 200 in podcallDdpcr, 400 in podcallThresholds) ;; Q=Parameter for calling outliers, multiplied by the IQR of amplitude values to determine extreme amplitude outliers (default 9; higher values yield stricter thresholds) ;; refwell=The well used as reference when calculating baseline shift between wells (default 1) ;; nrChannels=Number of channels used, set to 1 if no control channel is used (default 2) ;; targetChannel=The channel to be analyzed as the target channel (default 1) ;; controlChannel=The channel used for the control assay (default 2) ;; resultsToFile=Logical indicating whether to save the results table as a .csv file (default FALSE) ;; plots=Logical indicating whether to write plots to file (default FALSE) ;; resPath=Optional custom directory path for writing results files
- alternatives: None mentioned.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for analyzing DNA methylation ddPCR experiments performed on the Bio-Rad platform to set robust, automated thresholds and calculate normalized concentrations.
- pitfalls: All raw data files in the input directory must be from the same 96-well plate to avoid well coordinate duplicates. The software argument must be set correctly ("QuantaSoft" vs "QX Manager") because they format amplitude files and sample sheets differently (e.g., unequal number of lines to skip). To ensure reproducible results, set.seed() must be called before running because threshold setting includes random sampling of droplets.

workflows.name: ddpcr_methylation_analysis
workflows.intent: Run the complete PoDCall workflow to read raw ddPCR amplitude data, set thresholds, calculate concentrations, and visualize results.
input: amplitude_files.csv (raw amplitude values of droplets from each well of a 96-well plate, ending with _wellID_amplitude.csv)
Sample_names.csv (sample sheet containing Well, Sample, TargetType, and Target columns)
workflows.stages:
1. Import raw amplitude data from the directory using importAmplitudeData.
2. Import sample sheet information using importSampleSheet.
3. Calculate thresholds, positive droplet counts, and concentrations using podcallThresholds (or run the full workflow in one step using podcallDdpcr).
4. Visualize results using podcallChannelPlot, podcallScatterplot, podcallHistogram, or podcallMultiplot.
workflows.code:
thresholdTable <- podcallDdpcr(dataDirectory="path/to/data/",
                                software="QuantaSoft")

dataList <- importAmplitudeData(dataDirectory=path, skipLines=0)

sampleSheet <- importSampleSheet(sampleSheet=path, well_id=well_id,
                                software="QuantaSoft")

thresholdTable <- podcallThresholds(plateData=ampData)

podcallChannelPlot(channelData=ampData[[well_id]][,ch],
                    thr=thresholdTable[well_id, "thr_target"],
                    channel=ch,
                    plotId=plotTitle)

podcallScatterplot(channelData=ampData[[well_id]][,ch],
                    thr=thresholdTable[well_id, "thr_target"],
                    channel=ch,
                    plotId=plotTitle)

podcallHistogram(channelData=ampData[[well_id]][,ch],
                thr=thresholdTable[well_id, "thr_target"],
                channel=ch,
                plotId=plotTitle)

podcallMultiplot(plateData=ampData,
                thresholds=thresholdTable[names(ampData),], 
                channel=ch, colCh=1)
